Class Angular Distortion Index

Source: R/class-angular-distortion.R
class_angular_distortion_index.Rd

Compare how a class appears when viewed from another class. For each triplet, measure the cosine of the angle at the anchor between the rays to two observations from a different class.

Usage

class_angular_distortion_index(
  Xin,
  Xout,
  labels,
  n_triplets = NULL,
  triplets = NULL,
  ret_extra = FALSE
)

Arguments

Xin

Reference coordinates, as a dense numeric matrix or data frame with observations in rows.

Xout

Embedding coordinates for the same observations in the same order. Nonnumeric data-frame columns are ignored in both inputs.

labels

A vector without missing values, with one label per observation and at least two distinct labels. At least one class must have two members to supply endpoints.

n_triplets

Total number of triplets to sample. The default is ten times the number of observations.

triplets

Optional one-based plan such as sample_class_triplets(). The three indices must be distinct, and the endpoints must share a class different from the anchor's. When supplied, n_triplets is ignored.

ret_extra

Whether to return the plan, cosines, and directed class-pair summaries.

Value

The scalar index. With ret_extra = TRUE, returns a list with cadi, triplets, cosine_in, cosine_out, and pairs. pairs contains the observed directed class pairs, with columns anchor_class, endpoint_class, n_triplets, and cadi. Weighting the pair scores by their counts recovers the scalar.

Details

The index is the mean squared change in cosine divided by four, as in the authors' code. It ranges from 0 (agreement) to 1. A zero-length ray gives a cosine of zero. Quadra's sampler gives each eligible triplet equal probability, so class frequencies affect their representation in the overall score. Reuse a triplet plan for paired comparisons of embeddings.

The two directions of a class pair can have different distortions. Uniform scaling, translation, and orthogonal transformations preserve the angles. Angle agreement emphasizes relative angular spread. For example, compact classes can subtend small angles under several arrangements of their centers.

Scaling

Use the full coordinates and control the cost with n_triplets, the total number of sampled triplets (default 10 * N). The calculation processes coordinates in blocks and stores the triplet plan and cosines. Check the per-pair counts before interpreting a rare class direction.

Numerical failures

Nonfinite intermediate calculations cause an error. Extreme coordinate scales may affect accuracy even when the calculations remain finite.

References

Gunaratne, K., Kobourov, S., & Miller, J. (2026). Class Angular Distortion Index for Dimensionality Reduction. https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.00637

See also

label_trustworthiness_continuity(), roc_auc(), pr_auc()

Examples

x <- as.matrix(iris[, -5])
y <- prcomp(x, rank. = 2)$x
set.seed(42)
triplets <- sample_class_triplets(iris$Species, 1000)
class_angular_distortion_index(x, y, iris$Species, triplets = triplets)
#> [1] 0.002392586
